claims.claim: Enhanced POET keeps separate active population and archive
claims.evidence: poet_distributed/poet_algo.py:68 self.env_archive (every env ever created, OrderedDict), :71 self.archived_optimizers, :139 archive_optimizer(), :327 remove_oldest() archives when the active set exceeds max_num_envs

claims.claim: POET transfers policies between environments rather than only recording native performance
claims.evidence: poet_algo.py:164 transfer(); es.py:604 evaluate_transfer(): every source theta is evaluated in the target; with evaluate_proposal=True one ES step is proposed from it and re-evaluated; the best of direct/proposed becomes the proposal; es.py:250 pick_proposal(): the target adopts the foreign theta if it beats the checkpoint score (log field accept_theta_in_<id> records the source id)

claims.claim: PATA-EC: evaluate all agents on the environment, clip at lower/upper thresholds, rank-normalise, use the vector as the environment's characterisation
claims.evidence: es.py:586 update_pata_ec(): cap_score() clips each agent's return to [lower_bound, upper_bound]; scores over archived + active optimizers; self.pata_ec = compute_centered_ranks(raw_scores)
claims.precision: the clip bounds ARE the minimal-criterion bounds (mc_lower, mc_upper, poet_algo.py:296); the normalisation is centered ranks (the same transform ES uses on returns), so the vector lives in [-0.5, 0.5]

claims.claim: two environments are behaviourally different when they induce substantially different orderings
claims.evidence: poet_distributed/novelty.py: compute_novelty_vs_archive() = mean Euclidean distance to the k=5 nearest PATA-EC vectors over archive + active; euclidean_distance() pads the shorter vector with its last element when lengths differ (the archive grows, so older vectors are shorter) -- a quirk worth knowing before anyone reuses the distance

claims.claim: ASAL's open-endedness metric can be satisfied by embedding novelty without meaningful novelty
claims.evidence: asal_metrics.py:53 calc_open_endedness_score(z): kernel = z z^T, lower triangle k=-1, per-frame max similarity to ANY EARLIER frame, mean; minimised. Re-implemented in numpy with unit vectors (T=8, D=512, seed 0): static frame 0.8750, coherent slow drift 0.8654, 2-frame cycle 0.7500, iid random frames 0.0390. Pure noise is 22x 'more open-ended' than a coherent trajectory. Also: frame 0's row is all zeros, so the score is bounded by (T-1)/T of the mean. CAVEAT: this is a control on the METRIC, not on the pipeline -- CLIP does not map noise images to orthogonal vectors, so gaming the real system needs image-level experiments (TECHNE-107)

claims.claim: ASAL illumination score
claims.evidence: asal_metrics.py:66 calc_illumination_score(zs): mean nearest-neighbour similarity across parameter sets (diagonal -inf), minimised; the supervised target score is -mean diag(z_txt z^T) with prompts repeated over time

claims.claim: how much of TerraLingua's conceptual ancestry is deterministic provenance vs LLM post-hoc inference
claims.evidence: 006_artifact_philogeny.py docstring: two methods -- (1) 'hand annotation' = explicit mentions of previous artifacts in the agent's reasoning/observations/memory at creation time; (2) LLM inference (LLM_PROVIDER anthropic, LLM_MODEL claude-haiku-4-5, LLM_PHYLOGENY = True, BYNARY = True; prompts at :59 and :107 ask the model to pick ancestors from a candidate list with relationship type inspired_by / extends / modifies and a confidence). No logged parent or source-artifact id is read (grep for parent / source_id / created_from: none; the script reads ts_log action/observation/reasoning). So NEITHER method is deterministic provenance: method 1 is text matching on the agent's own reasoning, method 2 is a model's guess. The environment does not record 'which artifact this was copied from' at write time -- the second 'could have known but throws away' item
